src/flywheel/workflow.py:155-178 -- _latest_lifecycle_row SELECT; project blocked_requires_json into the returned tuple so task_state can populate the new field
src/flywheel/workflow.py:189-223 -- task_state classifier; thread the new field through into the returned TaskStatusRow

src/flywheel/harness.py -- the public recheck_blocked_lifecycle primitive and RecheckOutcome class added in the prerequisite task; import them into workflow.py rather than re-implementing predicate evaluation
constraints: Add subcommand `flywheel recheck-blocked` with: (a) default mode: scan `SELECT run_id, task_id FROM lifecycles WHERE status = 'interrupted' AND blocked_requires_json IS NOT NULL ORDER BY updated_at`; for each row, resolve its Task by walking the active tasks dir (use the existing build_status_rows / load_active_tasks plumbing) and call recheck_blocked_lifecycle; print one line per lifecycle of the form `<run_id>: unblocked` or `<run_id>: still blocked (<short summary of unmet predicates>)`. (b) `--run-id <id>` targets one lifecycle (skip the scan, just process that run_id; if missing or not blocked, print a clear message and exit 0). (c) `--dry-run` evaluates and reports without transitioning; pass dry_run=True to recheck_blocked_lifecycle so harness.recheck_attempted is emitted but harness.unblocked is NOT; prints `<run_id>: would unblock` or `<run_id>: still blocked (...)`.
Use the existing --db and --tasks-dir flag helpers (_add_common_db, _add_common_tasks_dir). Exit code 0 on success (including 'still blocked' cases); non-zero only on store/IO/load errors.

If a blocked lifecycle's task_id cannot be resolved to an active task file (e.g. task archived between block and recheck), skip it with a printed warning to stderr and continue the scan. Do not crash the batch.

Extend `flywheel status` text mode: for any row whose latest_status == Status.INTERRUPTED and whose blocked_requires_json is non-null, append `  blocked_on: <comma-joined per-predicate identifier list>` to that row's line (e.g. `blocked_on: command_grader=full-suite, file_exists=.workflow/lkg/.venv`). Rows without blocked_requires_json render unchanged.

Extend `flywheel status --json` output: include a `blocked_requires` key on each row whose underlying value is non-null. The value is the parsed list (list of dicts), not the raw JSON string. Rows whose value is null OMIT the key entirely (do not emit `null`) -- this matches the existing convention where unset fields are absent rather than null.

Update tests/test_workflow.py with coverage for: (a) recheck-blocked default scan, no blocked lifecycles -> exit 0, '(no blocked lifecycles)' or similar empty-state line; (b) default scan with one all-satisfied lifecycle -> transition applied, line says 'unblocked'; (c) default scan with one partially-satisfied lifecycle -> no transition, line says 'still blocked'; (d) --run-id targets one specific lifecycle and leaves others untouched; (e) --dry-run reports satisfied/unsatisfied without transitioning -- assert lifecycle status is still interrupted and harness.unblocked event is absent; (f) `flywheel status` text mode includes `blocked_on:` for interrupted rows with blocked_requires_json; (g) `flywheel status` text mode omits `blocked_on:` for interrupted rows without blocked_requires_json (the SIGINT-pause case); (h) `flywheel status --json` includes the parsed blocked_requires list for blocked rows and omits the key for others.

Update docs/loop.md harness behavior section (or a nearby section) with a one-paragraph note describing the `flywheel recheck-blocked` CLI subcommand and that it drives recheck_blocked_lifecycle from outside the loop. Keep it terse.
After editing Python, run mcp__ide__getDiagnostics on every .py file you touch and fix all Pylance errors before reporting verify -- treat them as build failures (see CLAUDE.md).
Commit the change with a Conventional Commits message (e.g. 'feat:') before reporting verify.
non_goals: Do not change the harness recheck behavior or the lifecycle state machine -- those landed in the prerequisite task.
Do not add concurrency / parallelism to the batch scan; sequential is intentional per spec Non-Functional Requirements.
Do not add a `flywheel ack-block` or `flywheel manual_ack` verb (deferred per spec Out of Scope).
Do not add an operator UI / dashboard (deferred per spec Out of Scope).
Do not register a top-level `flywheel` entrypoint script in pyproject.toml. The CLI is invoked via `uv run python -m flywheel.workflow recheck-blocked ...` consistent with all other subcommands.
edge_cases: Empty store (no lifecycles at all): `flywheel recheck-blocked` prints a clear empty-state line and exits 0.
A blocked lifecycle whose task file was archived after the block: the scan skips it with a stderr warning naming the run_id and the missing task_id, continues with the next.
Worker CWD differs from where the original attempt ran: predicates evaluate against the current CWD; do not attempt to enter the worktree (spec Out of Scope).
--dry-run on an all-satisfied lifecycle: prints `would unblock`, leaves status as interrupted, leaves blocked_requires_json intact, harness.recheck_attempted is emitted, harness.unblocked is not.
Default `flywheel status` for a lifecycle that was never blocked: no blocked_on line, no blocked_requires key in JSON.

A single lifecycle whose `blocked_requires_json` exists but is shorter than its tail of unmet predicates would suggest (e.g. one predicate of three is unmet): the `still blocked` summary names the unmet predicate(s) only, not all of them. Keep the summary short.
